thread.title: Analyzing Nvidia's Massive Run and Collapse (And What It Means for Other Stocks)

author: Day Trade Review
title: Analyzing Nvidia's Massive Run and Collapse (And What It Means for Other Stocks)
text:
- Fundamental Analysis - Technology Analyzing Nvidia's Massive Run and Collapse (And What It Means for Other Stocks) Day Trade Review Follow | Wednesday, 26 December 2018 10:29 (EST) Stocks are more volatile than ever, and some of the world's largest companies are taking major hits to their stock prices. Whenever this happens, speculation ensues. The talking heads bring up global trade, fed rates, lowered guidance, and other factors to justify these previously unexpected price drops.
While everyone focuses on a macro perspective, many forget to focus on how the stock market operates. You are essentially buying into a company, and that company has a value. That value isn't definitive, which is why stocks fluctuate in price. One investor may think Apple ( AAPL ) is worth $300/share while another may think it's only worth $100/share. What both of these investors can probably agree on is that Apple is worth more than $5/share and less than $2,000/share. Why is this relevant?
It proves that investors still believe in value, even if they're in favor of momentum and growth based strategies. Investors get so caught up in price predictions that they often forget the underlying companies have real values. Investors wait until stock prices experience higher volatility before they assign meaning to the move. You're more likely to hear that the market is crashing due to "insert reason here" than you were to hear that the market was overvalued a few months ago. Correlation doesn't equal causation.
NVDA Analysis Today we're going to look at Nvidia's ( NVDA ) numbers. We'll be using NVDA as an example, but this analysis can be applied to many top stocks that recently took a hit.
We'll be analyzing a few factors related to the company's fundamental value. Whether or not you are a value investor, you should recognize that a stock's price has to account for value.
Price The most obvious analysis of NVDA starts with price. The stock ran from $15 to $280 in five years, representing a price increase of nearly 2000%. Recently, the stock pulled back to $135, representing a price decrease of more than 50% from the highs.
Both the massive run and recent collapse are very noticeable on a chart.
When analyzed in isolation, this price drop may seem unwarranted, so let's add some more variables to the mix
Earnings and Revenue Analyzing a company's earnings and revenue is crucial to any fundamental analysis. If a company's value is increasing, the company should be making more money.
The chart below shows revenue (orange line) and EPS (red line) growth that correlates nicely with the price increase. As NVDA's price increases, the company is making more money and maintaining profitability.
When looking at the chart above, the price drop may seem unwarranted. In fact, it's the first clear divergence between price growth and revenue/EPS growth. Does that make NVDA a screaming buy? Let's look at one last factor.
Price/Earnings Ratio A stock's price/earnings ratio compares the stock's price to its earnings-per-share. While the P/E ratio is not the holy grail of value analysis, it's an easy ratio to look at to get a better understanding of a company's value.
In the previous chart, you saw that NVDA's revenue and earnings were increasing alongside the price. What you may not have noticed was the rate at which they were growing. While NVDA's stock price increased nearly 2000% in the past five years, revenues only increased about 175% and the EPS increased by roughly 670%.
The chart below compares NVDA's stock price (blue) to NVDA's P/E Ratio (orange).
Up until 2018, the P/E ratio was increasing alongside the price. To put this in perspective, if the stock price was increasing at the same rate as the company's earnings, the P/E ratio (orange) would be a flat line. Of course, current value isn't the only factor in a stock price, and P/E increases are not abnormal, but at a certain point reality hits.
Final Thoughts As the market goes wild and everyone scrambles to figure out what's going on, it can be helpful to incorporate a bit of the value perspective into your analysis. There are three potential outcomes to this analysis and they all provide actionable takeaways:
Stocks are becoming undervalued - This provides a great opportunity to buy at a discount Stocks have returned to fair value - This means the recent "correction" was justified and there may be a buying opportunity soon Stocks are still overvalued - This provides a good shorting opportunity or allows investors to wait for a further drop before entering positions
DISCLOSURE : I do not have a position in any stocks mentioned.
